- Consolidated monthly invoice: fine; we already support per-customer monthly consolidation.
- Tax: legal needs to confirm process for collecting exemption certificates; operations prefers to keep tax as a separate line item.

Lauren — can you draft a short redline mentioning net terms options and tax handling (accept certificate + tax-exempt stamping), and confirm whether we need a PO reference on invoices?
Priyom / Monica — want to lead the price/commit ask on whether we require the uplift for net 60 or if we can give net 60 without uplift for strategic reasons.

Thanks — I'll reply to Sanjay with a proposal once we sync.

David / team — draft redlines below for the order form / invoice annex. High level: accept consolidated monthly invoicing; propose net 45 standard or net 60 with payment security; accept tax-exempt certificate and remove tax where valid. Specifics: 

- Payment terms: "Customer shall pay invoices within forty-five (45) days of receipt. If Customer requires net sixty (60) (60) days), Redwood may agree in writing subject to (i) a one-time administrative fee equal to 0.5% of the invoice amount, or (ii) provision of a payment security instrument (e.g., purchase order with payment guarantee)."

- Invoices: "Redwood will issue consolidated monthly invoices to the billing contact designated in the Order Form. Each invoice will reference the applicable Purchase Order number provided by Customer."

- Taxes: "Unless Customer provides a valid tax exemption certificate for the relevant jurisdiction, Customer is responsible for all taxes. If a valid exemption certificate is supplied prior to the issuance of an invoice, Redwood will omit sales/use tax from that invoice. Redwood may request relevant tax documentation and reserves the right to collect taxes in accordance with applicable law."

- Minimum commit & pricing schedule: recommend locking in the committed spend column in Annex A: $250,000 annual minimum, billed monthly at the contracted rates, with tiered discounts applied per the pricing schedule. If Customer fails to meet committed spend by term end, shortfall will be payable as an invoice to be issued within 30 days after term end.

I can convert these into tracked redlines on the order form and Annex A. Any objections to the uplift for net 60 vs. accepting net 60 for strategic reasons?

Sanjay — thanks for sending the PO. We reviewed internally and can propose the following compromise so procurement can sign quickly: 

1) Net terms: Redwood standard for this committed order will be net 45 days. We can accept net 60 days only if Lumina (a) commits to the stated $250,000 annual minimum in Annex A and (b) provides either a purchase order with payment guarantee or accepts a one-time administrative uplift of 0.5% on the first invoice. Given Lumina's strategic value, we're willing to waive the uplift if you confirm the full annual commit and signed order form by EOD Friday.

2) Invoicing: We will issue a single consolidated monthly invoice to the address on the PO and will include the PO number on each invoice. We can also support sending invoices to procurement@luminahealth.com and cc your AP contact.

3) Taxes: Please send any applicable tax-exempt certificates to procurement@redwoodinference.com. If you provide a valid exemption certificate before we issue the invoice, we will omit sales/use tax for the jurisdictions covered. Otherwise taxes will be listed as a separate line item per applicable law.

Attached: InvoiceSchedule_AnnexA.xlsx (committed line and tiered pricing) and Redwood_W9.pdf. If Lumina is good with the commit + waived uplift, we can get countersigned today and route to DocuSign.

Next steps: 
- Sanjay: confirm whether you want to proceed with full commit (waive uplift) or prefer net 60 with the 0.5% uplift/security.
- Procurement: if you need W-9 or other compliance docs, let us know and we'll provide immediately.

Best,
David Kim
